(E-s3.11 NEW ITEM, full text) 11. Pre-registration versus competitiveness (written 27 Sep ~02:00Z, BEFORE any ladder or private score; do not rewrite after the private LB, add a dated 'post-private note' instead). WHAT THE RULES PROTECTED AGAINST: (a) choosing finals on 0.001 public differences measured on one embryo while 71% of the score sits on other embryos (R7 line; the READ TABLE made the 26 Sep 07:35Z finals read mechanical); (b) in-sample lab gains that do not transfer: the edge filter (+0.016 lab, 0/-0.001 LB), fork removers 0 for 5, overlap consensus (stopped by its own G-A, later confirmed -0.00143), head retrain (killed by the embryo-held-out test, +12% worse); (c) runtime and engineering failure near the deadline (safetail, byte-identical-when-off, sha dummies: no finals file errored or timed out); (d) post-hoc self-deception (ADDENDUM M labelled post-hoc and ignored). Speed was a side benefit: the pre-approved night slot put K2 into the 0.954 block at 26 Sep 00:01Z, 12th-15th of ~100 (ties go to the earlier submission), worth ~85 places over a late copy. WHAT THEY COST: (e) R9 banned retraining from 25 Sep 13:38Z to 29 Sep on evidence from the exp29 era (our retrains 0.920 and 0.937; model swaps 0 for 5; seed variance +-0.005 ~ the fine-tune gain). The ban was never re-tested on the x138 stack, where the 0.955+ route lay (own or distilled models plugged into x138), and it had no expiry or re-open trigger. ~22 of 30 weekly GPU-h were still unused at 26 Sep 21:5xZ. (f) R9's knob-ladder clause kept the four existing-knob rungs off the LB until the user lifted it at 26 Sep 20:33Z; by then their priors were <= +0.0003 public each, so the score cost is ~0, but the slot days were lost. (g) the bigger cost was ALLOCATION, not the rules: ~13 research rounds of ~20 agents plus the combo oracle went to inference-only post-processing whose GT-oracle ceiling (+0.0143 lab) was below 1.2x the bar, while the diagnosis 'the gap is detection/localisation' (83% of missing GT nodes absent upstream) was on record from round 3. HONEST ATTRIBUTION: the rules did not cause the lack of a better model; our retrains lost before R9 existed. What R9 removed was the option of ONE better-recipe retrain (distilled secondary, exp71) with idle quota; its expected value was uncertain (P(pass) ~0.25, +0.002..+0.003 public if it passes -> EV ~+0.0005..+0.0008 public, ~20-40 places at our density). The rule that protected the finals and the rule that froze exploration were written as one block and lifted as one block; that coupling is the process error. DO DIFFERENTLY NEXT COMPETITION: (1) Separate FINALS rules (strict, pre-registered, mechanical) from EXPLORATION rules (permissive, cheap gates). (2) Every ban gets an expiry and a named re-open trigger, e.g. 'a public engine > base with a model change', '>= 5 teams jump >= +0.003 over the public base block', 'idle GPU > 50% of the weekly quota with >= 3 days left'. (3) Measure the GT-oracle ceiling of a mechanism family before funding it; if the ceiling < 2x the bar, fund at most one round. (4) Fix a budget split in advance: >= 50% of GPU and agent time on the lever that owns the measured gap (here the detector) until D-7. (5) Build a leak-free embryo-held-out bed on day 1; every lab read in this competition was in-sample for at least one network. (6) Allow a small pre-registered public-probe budget for knob sign reads (e.g. 2 slots/week, sign-keeping only, never a finals input); on a deterministic kernel a public read is real, just narrow. (7) Scan the Code tab by score daily from week 1 (x138 was public 21 Sep; we found it 24 Sep 12:30Z). (8) Before the user goes offline, send numbered yes/no questions for every decision the night may need; 'do the same' is not a yes to a specific run.

findings.what: ROUTE-ROBUSTNESS READ (post-deadline, 0 GPU, uses the 29 Sep ~23:27Z public snapshot (timer bb224de9) and the final private board). Question it answers: did the route our R7/R9 rules blocked (public tuning, own models) keep its public margin on the private embryos? Groups from the public snapshot: C = teams displaying exactly 0.953 (x138-copy block, the control); A = 0.955-0.957 (the shoulder; ~120 teams: 63 + 38 + 19 at 22:46Z); B = 0.960-0.966 (the own-model band; 53 teams, 11 of them known jumpers from <= 0.954). Statistic per group g: transfer fraction f_g = median over g of (private_team - median private of C) / median over g of (public_team - 0.953). Pre-registered reading (one draw, learning only): f_A < 0.3 and f_B >= 0.5 -> 'public tuning did not transfer, model work did': R7 protected, R9 cost; f_A >= 0.5 -> public tuning transferred too, so the knob-ladder ban also cost us; f_B < 0.3 -> the model route did not transfer either, so the rules cost little. Our own point: f_us = (max(#37, #38) private - C median private) / 0.001. Arithmetic on size: A's public margin is +0.002..+0.004; under full transfer d_A ~ +0.002..+0.004, under none ~0; with ~120 teams the median is stable to well below 0.001 if private noise per team is ~0.002. Confounds (state them): a team's private is the max of its 2 selected files, not its best public file; C also contains near-copies with small tweaks; embryo mix differs. Cost ~1 eng-h. Cheapest honest gate: group definitions and thresholds committed before the first private score (with R14L-6).

findings.what: RULE-REGISTER TEMPLATE for the next competition (process, text only). Each rule gets five fields: PURPOSE (which failure it protects against: public overfit / in-sample lab / runtime / post-hoc), SCOPE (finals vs exploration), EXPIRY (date), RE-OPEN TRIGGER (observable event), COST METER (what we give up, logged daily: idle GPU-h, unused slots, agent-rounds spent on families whose oracle ceiling < bar). Retro-test on this competition's log (cheap, ~1 eng-h, after 29 Sep): would each trigger have fired, and when? Candidates: T1 'a public engine above the base with a model change' (y3uanm's distilled secondary was known by 25 Sep 22:23Z, R3S-6); T2 '>= 5 teams jump >= +0.003 above the public base block in one window' (seen 26 Sep 20:01Z; check older intel snapshots); T3 'idle GPU > 50% of the weekly quota with >= 3 days left' (true at 26 Sep 21:5xZ: 07:55/30 h used). If T1 or T3 fires before 26 Sep 12:00Z in the retro-test, the lesson 'R9 needed a re-open trigger' is supported; if none fires before R8, the ban cost less than s3.11 claims and s3.11 gets a dated correction.
